guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep user-visible reports distinct from machine-readable evidence and surface the report directly in the conversation.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: ai-finish writes deterministic JSON/Markdown evidence, then renders the bounded Outcome to stdout for the agent to relay in the active conversation.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Do not treat continuing execution authority as evidence that a particular human reviewed an Outcome.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The report boundary says archive is explicit after direct reporting, and the documented limitation states that CLI output cannot prove human identity, receipt, reading, or approval.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Preserve the canonical archive → PR → merge → closure sequence after the active reporting point.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The default Make and CLI entrypoints omit archive; ARCHIVE=true is the separate transition after the active direct-report boundary.

scenarioCoverage.reason: The report chrome renders in each supported locale while machine evidence remains unchanged.

risk.detail: Active Outcome generation, explicit archive separation, and installer parity affect lifecycle evidence; focused and full quality verification are required.

observedIssues.title: Implementation preparation checkpoint was recorded after the first focused TDD edit
observedIssues.description: The required ai-prepare-implementation command was not run before the first local test and source edits. Work stopped, the checkpoint was recorded, and the deviation is retained rather than presented as compliant history.
observedIssues.followUp: The existing command records the boundary but cannot reconstruct an already-edited working tree. Future agents must invoke it before any TDD edit; this limitation remains visible in the Outcome.

observedIssues.title: Active Outcome artifacts were not bound consistently across lifecycle gates
observedIssues.description: A successful active Outcome made an explicit archive retry fail because scope and diff ownership gates did not recognize the deterministic artifacts.
observedIssues.followUp: Future Contracts declare the artifacts and legacy Contracts receive the same narrow deterministic binding in both gates.

observedIssues.title: Contract scope refinement invalidated the recorded before_edit checkpoint
observedIssues.description: The first full finish correctly rejected the active Summary because its before_edit checkpoint hash no longer matched the refined Contract. No stale checkpoint will be reused; the canonical preflight and prepare command must record the current Contract before verification restarts.
observedIssues.followUp: The renewed checkpoint is necessarily later than the first implementation edit and therefore does not erase RFE-108-ISSUE-001; both deviations remain visible in the direct Outcome.

observedIssues.title: ARCHIVE=true leaked from an outer lifecycle command into nested adopter Make runs
observedIssues.description: An explicit archive invocation propagated ARCHIVE through GNU Make's MAKEFLAGS and MAKEOVERRIDES into pytest-created adopter repositories. Their ai-finish commands therefore selected archive mode unexpectedly, changing lifecycle test behavior.
observedIssues.followUp: The ai-finish recipe now translates the current invocation's ARCHIVE value into the Python flag, then removes ARCHIVE, MAKEFLAGS, and MAKEOVERRIDES before any nested command can inherit them. The generic environment cleaner blocks the same variables for direct subprocesses.

observedIssues.title: Derived Japanese assessment was generated before the final source formatting change
observedIssues.description: The Japanese capability report binds source digests. A later formatting-only change to a covered test made the report stale, and the full quality gate correctly rejected it.
observedIssues.followUp: The final verification sequence now formats and validates source first, then regenerates all digest-bound derived evidence immediately before the full gate.

residualRisks.detail: Language selection renders deterministic report chrome only; it cannot authenticate a chat recipient or prove that a human read or approved the report.

reviewReadiness.reason: Required verification or known-unknown evidence is incomplete.
expectedReviewFocus: Default ai-finish must retain active evidence and never archive implicitly.
Explicit archive retry must pass scope and ownership gates for both new and legacy Contracts.
Installed Runtime must include the multilingual renderer and preserve the Make entrypoint boundary.

knownGaps: A local command can render and print the report, but it cannot establish the identity, receipt, reading, or approval of the human in the conversation.
overclaimPrevention: Do not report completion for checks or behavior that were not verified.

checks.reason: The serial plan and bidirectional traceability now record RFE-108 as the successor before dependent work resumes.
Contract acceptance, Summary scope, active Outcome artifacts, and direct-report boundary describe the same lifecycle.
The root and installed Runtime entrypoints use the same default active-report and explicit archive command boundary.
English, Chinese, and Japanese report chrome is tested while the underlying evidence remains one deterministic record.
The remaining limitation is explicit: rendered output does not prove a human recipient's identity, receipt, reading, or approval.
